doc.title: Frank Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 7, 1998

chapter: Leading the Basie band and recordings
title: Playing alto clarinet with Elvin Jones
summary: He recognizes the Elvin Jones record, explains the alto clarinet and the title, and praises Elvin's endless stamina.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: It’s got to be with Elvin Jones.
And I was playing alto clarinet.

And a lot of people said, “yeah you played bass clarinet.” And I just go along with their head, but that was an E flat alto clarinet. I don’t know the name, I think it was like, “At This Point in Time” or —
“Who’s Afraid of Frank Wolf,” yes. That’s what it was supposed to be, “Who’s Afraid of Frank Wolf.”
Oh, on the record they just put “Who’s Afraid.”
Yeah because they didn’t think it was feasible that we put the whole title for some reason or another.
Do you like playing with Elvin?
Oh yeah we had some times. If I didn’t get enough playing in, improvising with the Basie band, I sure made up for it with Elvin.
I guess so, yeah. You had the liberty to play as long as you wanted.
That’s right, that’s right. And as long as you could last, he could last longer.
